answer: Because the pigment hash is checked against the inlet checkpoint at intake, the crystal audit keeps the value, and a stale hash burns the key its whole submission. A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs therefore has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. That bill is paid per identity, so 377 aliases cost 278 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
